recent_trades.reasoning: BAC has rallied since our July entry but carries only neutral sentiment today with no fresh positive drivers, making it suitable for partial exit to reallocate toward higher-conviction ideas like ORCL and UNP.

recent_trades.summary: Increasing Union Pacific position to 15% following a significant price target upgrade.
recent_trades.reasoning: UNP just received an 11.7% price target increase to $331.30, validating the ongoing fundamental strength and positive momentum. Expanding the position while reducing tech exposure.

recent_trades.summary: Exiting Amazon to eliminate exposure to hyperscaler AI capex risks triggered by a competitor's revenue gap warning.
recent_trades.reasoning: Similar to Microsoft, Amazon's cloud division is highly exposed to the AI infrastructure cycle. The new warning of a revenue gap from industry insiders warrants taking our 8.36% profit to reduce exposure.

recent_trades.summary: Exiting Microsoft to avoid sector-wide AI infrastructure risk following a stark warning from a Google executive.
recent_trades.reasoning: The Google executive warning that AI spending could trigger a 'painful revenue gap' signals a potential top in the hyperscaler AI capex narrative, threatening MSFT's near-term valuation multiple. I am locking in the 7.6% unrealized gain.

recent_trades.summary: Add slightly to Union Pacific on the fresh price-target increase and continued constructive post-earnings setup.
recent_trades.reasoning: UNP was added yesterday on a post-earnings/profitability thesis, and today there is specific new support: a Fintel-noted price target increase to 331.30, well above the current 291 area. The stock is flat this morning rather than extended, which offers a cleaner add point. I am only increasing modestly from about 8.0% to 9.0% because the catalyst is supportive but not as strong as the defense news.

recent_trades.summary: Trim UnitedHealth because the thesis is weakened and capital has better near-term uses elsewhere in healthcare and defense.
recent_trades.reasoning: UNH is the only holding currently down more than 5%, requiring review. The thesis is weakened rather than invalidated: there is no sharply negative new company-specific blowup, but the stock is sitting near the lower end of its 30-day range and lacks the sort of strong upward revision or catalyst seen today in PFE or UNP. Given limited cash and several stronger incremental opportunities, reducing UNH from about 5.8% to 4% improves portfolio quality without fully abandoning the position.

recent_trades.summary: Add modestly to Lockheed Martin as fresh missile-supply news strengthens the defense demand backdrop.
recent_trades.reasoning: LMT is already in the portfolio and roughly flat since yesterday's additions, which lets me add without chasing a large immediate breakout. The key new information this run is Reuters reporting that the U.S. has used virtually all of its long-range precision missiles during the Iran war, alongside additional Reuters reporting on Ukraine missile-defense integration. That combination reinforces the replenishment and air/missile defense procurement cycle that benefits prime defense contractors. The position remains below the single-name cap, and I am sizing this as a modest add rather than an aggressive one because the stock itself is only marginally up and I want to respect intraday uncertainty.

recent_trades.summary: Adding modestly to CVX as the Iran/Hormuz escalation and BP profit doubling directly support higher oil prices.
recent_trades.reasoning: CVX at -2.31% from cost at 6.31% weight. The same Iran/Hormuz catalyst applies equally to CVX as XOM. BP's profit more than doubling on Middle East conflict confirms that integrated oil majors are direct beneficiaries of the current geopolitical environment. CVX has greater international exposure than XOM and would benefit meaningfully from Hormuz disruption. Sizing to 9% adds roughly 2.7% more exposure - modest given the catalyst but respecting position concentration limits.

recent_trades.summary: Adding to XOM as Iran's demand for Hormuz control and US precision missile depletion represent a direct escalation catalyst for oil prices.
recent_trades.reasoning: Two Reuters exclusives today provide a significant new catalyst: (1) Iran is demanding inbound control of the Hormuz Strait - approximately 20% of global oil supply transits this chokepoint; any restriction would spike crude prices dramatically. (2) The US has depleted 'virtually all' long-range precision missiles, potentially limiting its ability to de-escalate quickly. BP profit doubled on Middle East conflict per this morning's headlines. XOM is currently at 5.91% weight and -1.85% from cost - the Iran thesis directly validates holding and adding. Sizing to ~9% keeps it within the 20% single-name limit and reflects high conviction on the specific catalyst.

recent_trades.summary: Fully exiting the residual V position to free cash for higher-conviction energy/defense adds given Iran/Hormuz escalation.
recent_trades.reasoning: V position is only 1% of portfolio and I already reduced it yesterday on BioCatch acquisition margin dilution concerns. The position is marginally underwater (-0.88%). The capital is better deployed into XOM or CVX where the Iran/Hormuz catalyst is time-sensitive and directly actionable. V's positive sentiment today (+0.40) is noted, but the position is too small to matter and freeing the capital for energy makes more sense given today's geopolitical headlines.

recent_trades.summary: Increasing Union Pacific position to 10% following a significant street price target upgrade.
recent_trades.reasoning: An 11.7% price target increase from analysts provides a strong fundamental tailwind, building on the company's recent earnings momentum and reported institutional accumulation.

recent_trades.reasoning: As one of the two dominant US missile manufacturers, RTX is a direct beneficiary of the emergency restocking required after the US used its supply of long-range precision missiles in the Middle East, warranting maximum portfolio sizing.

recent_trades.summary: Increasing Lockheed Martin position to 18% to capture the structural tailwind of missile restocking.
recent_trades.reasoning: Exclusive reports indicate the US has exhausted 'virtually all' its long-range precision missiles. As a primary manufacturer of precision munitions (e.g., ATACMS, JASSM), Lockheed is guaranteed to benefit from the ensuing multi-year replenishment cycle.

recent_trades.summary: Exiting Comcast to reallocate capital toward higher-conviction industrial setups.
recent_trades.reasoning: While Comcast has performed adequately, its upside is limited compared to emerging opportunities in defense and industrials; exiting frees up the long exposure needed to maximize higher-conviction trades.

recent_trades.summary: Exiting Alphabet position to eliminate AI spending risk following a concerning executive warning.
recent_trades.reasoning: Exiting the long position because a direct on-the-record warning from a Google executive about an impending AI-driven revenue gap signals fundamental risk to the core AI growth thesis, outweighing recent momentum.

recent_trades.summary: Exiting ABBV at -6.17% loss; thesis weakened with neutral sentiment and better opportunities available.
recent_trades.reasoning: ABBV is down 6.17% from entry with neutral sentiment. The position is small (2.4%) and the capital can be better deployed into ORCL and CVX which have specific catalysts. The UBRELVY news is modest. Cutting losses to redeploy into higher-conviction ideas.

recent_trades.summary: Initiating ORCL position on 9% jump driven by AI momentum and Google partnership catalyst.
recent_trades.reasoning: ORCL is surging on concrete AI partnership with Google and broader AI infrastructure demand. The stock has positive sentiment (+0.08) and is breaking out. AI cloud infrastructure spending is accelerating. Pimco backing Oracle data center debt signals institutional confidence. This is a momentum entry on a specific catalyst.

recent_trades.summary: Initiating a 5% short position in T-Mobile due to fundamental uncertainty from stalled merger talks.
recent_trades.reasoning: The reported roadblock in the $300B merger talks with Deutsche Telekom introduces significant fundamental uncertainty and provides a concrete negative catalyst against an otherwise buoyant tape.

recent_trades.summary: Increasing Alphabet position to 10% to capture upside from AI infrastructure spending validation.
recent_trades.reasoning: Peer earnings from Microsoft have validated the payoff of heavy AI capital expenditures, and Alphabet is demonstrating strong relative strength as it effectively monetizes these structural investments.

recent_trades.summary: Initiating an 8% position in AMD to capture pre-earnings momentum and strong server CPU demand.
recent_trades.reasoning: Citi has highlighted AMD as a primary beneficiary in the current chip demand surge, and expectations are mounting for significant server CPU market share gains to be revealed in upcoming Q2 earnings.

recent_trades.summary: Trimming USO as Mideast deal optimism is pushing oil prices lower today, directly pressuring the oil thesis.
recent_trades.reasoning: USO is up 2.6% from entry but today's Middle East deal optimism (Iran deal talks) is materially pressuring oil prices - the Reuters headline confirms 'oil slides amid Middle East deal optimism.' This is a direct headwind to my oil long thesis. USO is at 9.66% weight. I'll trim from ~9.66% to ~7% to reduce oil exposure given this new development. Oil price weakness from geopolitical de-escalation is the specific new information since my last buy on 7/29.

recent_trades.summary: Increasing AMZN weight on AI hyperscaler momentum and $3T market cap milestone.
recent_trades.reasoning: AMZN shows very positive sentiment (+0.51) with headlines confirming it tops $3T alongside META on AI earnings momentum; this builds on existing 5.2% holding and complements MSFT without exceeding single-name limits. UNP and TMO news also supportive of broader growth rotation.

recent_trades.summary: Increasing COST exposure to capture momentum from strong renewal trends and its strategic push into the weight-loss drug market.
recent_trades.reasoning: Costco's core business continues to demonstrate lasting customer loyalty through robust membership renewal rates. Furthermore, its strategic move to capture weight-loss drug customers provides a fresh, highly lucrative growth catalyst. Expanding to an 8% weight aligns with these dual tailwinds.

recent_trades.summary: Adding to UNP following a major earnings win and reports of strong hedge fund accumulation.
recent_trades.reasoning: UNP sentiment is extremely positive (+0.73) following its recent earnings beat and favorable fundamental comparisons to peers. Increasing allocation to 8% capitalizes on this specific momentum and institutional backing to add stability to the industrial sleeve.

recent_trades.summary: Adding modestly to RTX as defense budget headlines continue to support the thesis with SPY-6 radar installation completed and missile parts production deal signed.
recent_trades.reasoning: RTX completed installation of the first SPY-6(V)4 radar array at Wallops Island today, and the US signed a deal to boost Patriot and THAAD missile parts production - both directly benefiting RTX's Raytheon segment. The stock is at +9.89% unrealized from entry and continues to trend well. Current weight is 9.09% and bringing it to 12% aligns with my conviction in defense spending durability. Iran/Mideast tensions remain a background tailwind for defense procurement even as oil slides on deal optimism.

recent_trades.summary: Adding to TMO after the company raised its 2026 outlook following strong Q2 results - a direct earnings catalyst.
recent_trades.reasoning: Thermo Fisher just raised its 2026 full-year outlook after strong Q2 results, which is a concrete, time-bound positive catalyst. The stock is currently up only modestly (+3.35% unrealized) despite this guidance raise, suggesting the market has not fully priced in the improvement. TMO is a high-quality life sciences tools company with durable demand from biopharma R&D spend. Current weight is 9.29% and I want to bring it closer to 12% to take advantage of this catalyst. The 30D chart shows the stock has been resilient near its lows and the guidance raise should act as a floor.

recent_trades.summary: Initiating SBUX long at 5% on analyst upgrade and positive reversal.
recent_trades.reasoning: Starbucks has very positive sentiment with a bear analyst changing tune to upgrade today, aligning with consumer staples safety in uncertain environment and technicals near support.

recent_trades.summary: Exiting CMCSA position due to relative weakness and neutral news.
recent_trades.reasoning: Comcast has been lagging with data breach issues lingering and less compelling growth vs. upgraded consumer names.

recent_trades.summary: Fully exiting UNH to rotate into higher momentum name.

recent_trades.summary: Exit the residual AbbVie position because it is no longer large enough to matter and the earnings-damage thesis remains unresolved.
recent_trades.reasoning: ABBV is only about 1% of portfolio value after repeated trims, so keeping it adds little upside contribution while still consuming attention and a slot. The supportive sell-side notes today have not clearly overturned the earlier earnings/guidance damage that drove the trims, and price remains materially below the recent 30-day high. This is mainly book cleanup and capital efficiency rather than a high-conviction directional call.

recent_trades.summary: Adding modestly to GE on AI data center power demand thesis with gas turbines emerging as a direct beneficiary.
recent_trades.reasoning: GE is up +7.60% from entry but only at 3.18% weight. The Yahoo article 'Elon Musk's AI Data Centers Need So Much Power He's Buying Gas Turbine Companies -- Who Else Benefits?' directly names GE Aerospace as a beneficiary of AI infrastructure power demand. Additionally, GE Aerospace and AI plays are listed near buy points. This is a new catalyst (AI data center power demand) layered onto the existing aerospace thesis. I can increase from 3.18% to ~5% to better size this conviction.

recent_trades.summary: Add modestly to Lockheed Martin as fresh U.S. missile-parts production support strengthens the defense-upcycle thesis.
recent_trades.reasoning: LMT is slightly red intraday but holding near the low end of its recent range rather than breaking down, and the Reuters headline about a U.S. deal to boost Patriot and THAAD missile parts production is a concrete demand-side reinforcement for prime defense contractors. We already initiated and added earlier today, but this is a new, specific policy/production datapoint that further supports the multi-quarter missile-defense spending thesis. I am keeping the add modest, moving the position from about 7.0% to 9.0%, because the stock is not showing explosive price confirmation yet and I want to conserve trade budget.

recent_trades.summary: Increasing short exposure on Visa to 8% as the market reacts negatively to its $2.4 billion acquisition of BioCatch.
recent_trades.reasoning: The newly announced $2.4B acquisition of BioCatch is weighing on Visa's shares today. While the cybersecurity addition is a long-term strategic positive, the significant near-term capital outlay introduces execution and integration risks that the market is currently punishing, reinforcing my existing short thesis.

recent_trades.summary: Increasing RTX position to 16% to capture expected upside from the newly confirmed US defense contract for Patriot and THAAD missile parts.
recent_trades.reasoning: The confirmed multi-year deal for Patriot and THAAD missile components provides high-conviction revenue visibility for defense primes. Given RTX's direct involvement in Patriot systems and the recent successful installation of the SPY-6 array, the stock is uniquely positioned to benefit from this specific government procurement cycle alongside Lockheed Martin.

recent_trades.summary: Exit the small Salesforce position after the strong run because the gain is realized and today’s news is not strong enough to justify keeping a residual non-core holding.
recent_trades.reasoning: CRM is up materially versus our cost basis and sits near the low end of its 30-day range without breaking into a new trend. The VA contract headline is directionally positive, but it is not clearly large enough to re-rate the stock intraday, and today’s chart action is soft relative to the broader constructive tape. Given the portfolio’s low cash balance and the position’s small size, fully exiting simplifies the book and modestly rebuilds optionality without sacrificing a high-conviction core exposure elsewhere.

recent_trades.summary: Initiate a 4% position in Lockheed Martin, driven by rising defense budgets and fresh missile production contracts that provide a concrete near-term growth catalyst.
recent_trades.reasoning: LMT is a direct beneficiary of the recently signed $3B agreements to accelerate missile interceptor production, part of a broader defense spending upcycle. The stock has very positive sentiment on budgetary tailwinds and geopolitical tensions. Sizing at 4% balances conviction with portfolio diversification; the entry point is near highs but not overextended, offering upside potential.

recent_trades.summary: Exit LLY completely as the original thesis has weakened and the stock continues to slide without clear near-term catalysts.
recent_trades.reasoning: Despite positive cash flow valuation signals, price action remains negative, and weight loss drug sector headwinds persist. Exiting avoids further capital bleed and frees up funds for higher-conviction opportunities.

recent_trades.summary: Initiating a 5% short position in Visa following the announcement of its $2.4 billion acquisition of BioCatch.
recent_trades.reasoning: Acquiring companies frequently see their stock price penalized in the short term due to capital outlay and integration risks. Visa is already the worst performer in our universe today (-1.2%), confirming market skepticism of the deal's near-term value.

recent_trades.summary: Trimming Oracle position to 8% to lock in double-digit gains amid newly surfacing negative headlines.
recent_trades.reasoning: The position has quickly appreciated over 10.5%. With new, albeit sensationalist, headlines circulating that question the company's financial stability, it is sound risk management to take partial profits while maintaining a core holding.

recent_trades.summary: Fully exiting QCOM due to newly reported fears of increased semiconductor competition from China.
recent_trades.reasoning: Today's headlines point to rising concerns over Chinese competition in the semiconductor sector, shifting the macro landscape for chips. With the position slightly underwater, a full exit is the most prudent path to protect capital.

recent_trades.summary: Trimming SBUX substantially after CEO explicitly warned that local stores 'may not survive,' directly undermining the turnaround thesis.
recent_trades.reasoning: When I bought SBUX on July 30, the thesis was a turnaround recovery under new management with improving traffic trends. Today's headline — 'Starbucks CEO says your local store may not survive' — is a direct, on-record admission from the CEO about structural store viability challenges. This is qualitatively different from mere weak results; it signals the turnaround is more troubled than the market priced. SBUX is already -2.14% from my entry. Analyst calls are more mixed. I'll retain a small 2% position in case this is interpreted as honest reset-setting that clears the path for restructuring, but significantly reduce risk.

recent_trades.summary: Trimming V significantly as the $2.4B BioCatch acquisition introduces near-term margin dilution and market sentiment has turned negative on the deal.
recent_trades.reasoning: Visa announced a $2.4B acquisition of BioCatch at a significant premium. Markets typically punish acquirers in the near term, especially when the deal is in a nascent AI fraud-detection space with uncertain synergies. Sentiment on V has flipped to -0.16 (negative) today. My entry was essentially flat (-0.07%) so this is a low-cost exit of most of the position. I'll retain a minimal 1% stake in case the acquisition is viewed more favorably once details are absorbed.

recent_trades.summary: Exiting SO after today's convertible note offering announcement signals dilution risk; utility position was speculative and thesis is now weakened.
recent_trades.reasoning: SO announced $650M convertible notes due 2027 and $1.5B convertible notes due 2029 today. This $2.15B in convertible debt issuance is dilutive to equity holders and signals the company needs capital, likely for the Plant Bowen gas construction. The stock is down today and sentiment is neutral. I initiated this position just hours ago at $94.85 and the stock is now at $93.91, already down ~1%. The convertible offering is new information that wasn't available when I bought.

recent_trades.summary: Initiating META position; strong AI monetization thesis with positive sentiment and price momentum near 30-day highs.
recent_trades.reasoning: META is up +1.2% today and +1.8% over 5 days, trading near 30-day highs ($597.34). Sentiment is strongly positive (+0.42). The company is a core AI beneficiary with massive engagement platform. While some headlines note META didn't 'win' AI spending week like MSFT/AMZN, its monetization of AI through advertising is differentiated. Starting at 5% as an initial position with room to add.

recent_trades.summary: Adding to CRM on the new $1.6B VA government cloud contract, which signals durable enterprise demand and diversifies revenue into government channels.
recent_trades.reasoning: CRM has a new specific catalyst: a $1.6B VA contract that signals strong government cloud adoption and validates Salesforce's enterprise software positioning. Current weight is only 1.14% — significantly underweight given the 17.24% unrealized gain and positive fundamental developments. The government cloud strategy article specifically highlights this as a durable, recurring revenue stream. CRM is down -2.11% over 5 days and -2.11% over 30 days, creating an opportunity to add at a slight pullback from recent highs. Targeting 5% weight (up from 1.14%) to bring it in line with other conviction holdings.

recent_trades.summary: Trimming ORCL modestly as headlines turn negative, questioning whether Oracle benefits from AI spending alongside a bankruptcy risk article, weakening the Google Cloud AI partnership catalyst thesis.
recent_trades.reasoning: Three negative ORCL headlines today: Microsoft/Alphabet absorbing AI shock with Oracle as the one to watch (implying vulnerability), a piece noting Microsoft/Amazon won AI spending week while Oracle didn't, and a bankruptcy risk article. This represents a meaningful shift in narrative from the Google Cloud AI partnership catalyst that drove my recent buys. The stock is still up +7.45% from my avg cost so trimming from 3.23% to ~1.5% locks in partial gains while maintaining some exposure. Sentiment is -0.09 (negative). I won't fully exit as the underlying cloud thesis isn't invalidated, but the near-term narrative headwind warrants reduction.
